anomalies.observed: C54 is a 0.1nF (100pF) capacitor on the +5V rail to GND. Its copied metadata fields (Field4-Field8, 'Part Description 0.1uF 10% 16V Ceramic Capacitor X7R') describe a 0.1uF part, not a 100pF one.
anomalies.expected: A +5V bulk-decoupling position should carry a 0.1uF ceramic like the other decoupling capacitors (C6, C36, C47 share the same copied fields and are 0.1uF). A 100pF capacitor provides almost no high-frequency decoupling for the 5V rail that feeds the CM4 and the LED and CAN loads.

evidence.quote: Field6=RM EMK105 B7104KV-F, Field7=TAIYO YUDEN EUROPE GMBH, Part Description=	0.1uF 10% 16V Ceramic Capacitor X7R 0402 (1005 Metric)

anomalies.impact: Weakened high-frequency decoupling on the +5V rail, which can cause supply noise and instability on the 5V consumers.

anomalies.observed: The LTC4412 PowerPath PMOS Q1 has its source (pin 2) on +5V, the output net, and its drain (pin 3) on USBC_VBUS_IN, the USB input. The LTC4412 VIN (U6.1) is on USBC_VBUS_IN and SENSE (U6.6) is on +5V.
anomalies.expected: In an LTC4412 ideal-diode OR-ing stage, the P-channel MOSFET source is the input (VIN side) and its drain is the load (SENSE side). The body diode must conduct from the USB input to the 5V output, and reverse-current blocking depends on this orientation.

evidence.quote: Q1 | Q_PMOS_GSD | Package_TO_SOT_SMD:SOT-23 | Device:Q_PMOS_GSD | P-MOSFET transistor, gate/source/drain
USBC_VBUS_IN [High Power] : J3.A4(VBUS,passive) J3.A9(VBUS,passive) J3.B4(VBUS,passive) J3.B9(VBUS,passive) Q1.3(D,passive) R11.1(passive) R64.2(2,passive) U25.5(VBUS,passive) U6.1(VIN,power_in)

anomalies.impact: If the source and drain are swapped, the PMOS body diode points the wrong way and the reverse-current protection the spec calls for is not achieved, so power can flow from the 5V rail back toward USB.

anomalies.observed: Both isolated CAN transceivers have GND1 (pin 4) and GND2 (pin 5) on the same GND net. The motherboard has no separate isolated ground net.
anomalies.expected: An isolated CAN transceiver (CA-IS3050G / ISO1050 class) should have its bus-side ground (GND2) isolated from the logic-side ground (GND1). Tying them together removes the galvanic isolation the design intends.

evidence.quote: GND [High Power] : ... U10.4(GND1,power_in) U10.5(GND2,power_in) U11.4(GND1,power_in) U11.5(GND2,power_in)
U11 | isolator | Package_SO:SOIC-8_7.5x5.85mm_P1.27mm | Interface_CAN_LIN:ISO1050DUB | Isolated CAN Transceiver, SOP-8
two isolated CAN buses (`CAN0`, `CAN1`), each driven by its own MCP2515 SPI CAN controller

anomalies.impact: The CAN buses are not galvanically isolated, so ground loops or faults on the bus can reach the logic side of the board.
